subject: Audit & Access Logs: Forensic Exports, Retention Windows, and Practical Limitations
messages:
From: Jake Miller <jake.miller@greenbridgehealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: sec@greenbridgehealth.com
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: audit log export for security incident forensic review

Hi Laura —

We’re doing a quick forensic triage after a suspicious access pattern on our test environment and need to pull a set of audit/access logs covering 2026-07-15 to 2026-07-22. Can you confirm:

- What export formats you can provide (CSV/NDJSON/Parquet)?
- Is there a maximum contiguous window we can export on-demand?
- Typical SLA for producing a bulk export?
- Whether exports include the full request/response metadata (caller IPs, region, model id, route id, token counts, and any masking applied)?
- If Redwood provides a signed manifest (hash + signature) for chain-of-custody?

We also need to confirm whether you can route the exported data to our S3 in us-east-1 and whether any PII is redacted by default. If there’s a short checklist or playbook you can send, that’d help greatly.

Thanks — want to get this turned around quickly.

Jake Miller
Security Lead, Greenbridge Health
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Jake Miller <jake.miller@greenbridgehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: audit log export for security incident forensic review

Jake —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by specifics and export/playbook attachments.

High-level: we can provide exports in CSV, NDJSON, or Parquet; the default on-demand export UI/API supports up to a 30-day contiguous window. For wider date ranges (one-off bulk archives beyond 30 days) we initiate a managed archive job that typically completes within 24–72 hours depending on size. We can deliver exports to a customer-owned S3 bucket in us-east-1 (or other region) via a pre-signed PUT or by provisioning a temporary, write-only presigned URL.

Details:
- Format & fields: ex-
  - CSV/NDJSON/Parquet available.
  - Standard fields exported: event_timestamp, principal_id, internal_user_id (hashed), caller_ip, region, model_id, route_id, request_headers (stripped of auth tokens), request_body_meta (size/token_count), response_status, kv_cache_events (presence/size), storage_refs (when relevant), and event_id.
  - We do not include raw prompt text by default for hosted accounts unless Customer chooses to enable long-term prompt retention in the contract (default is to exclude prompt content for PII minimization). When prompt_text is enabled, it is included in exports as a separate field.

- On-demand window limits: up to 30 contiguous days via the console/API. Requests for narrower windows are faster and generally returned within minutes to a few hours.

- Bulk archive requests (forensic or legal discovery): We treat these as managed jobs — lead time 24–72 hours, depending on export size; we will provide estimated completion in the job creation response. For very large historical pulls (>1TB), expect multi-day windows and we provide streaming to the target bucket.

- Chain-of-custody & signed manifest: yes — we produce a manifest.json with SHA256 hashes for each file plus a Redwood-signed signature (x509) that you can use for verification. I’ve attached a signed_export_manifest_example.json as a sample.

- PII & redaction: by default for hosted accounts we redact or exclude high-sensitivity fields (raw prompt_text, credit card numbers detected by detectors, auth tokens). We can enable a redaction-preserve export (i.e., include original text) under a dedicated contract with documented access controls and an audit trail.

- Evidence integrity: exports include file-level checksums and a compact audit of export events (who requested, job id, timestamps, delivery target). We also retain an internal export audit trail for 1 year.

- Retention policy summary:
  - Hosted (standard): access/audit logs retained for 90 days in hot storage; 90–365 days retained in cold storage depending on account tier and add-ons.
  - Dedicated: configurable retention up to 5 years depending on contract and storage commitment.
  - Private (customer-managed): retention is controlled by the customer deployment; Redwood provides tools to perform exports and deletion commands but retention is subject to on-prem/VPC configuration.

- Deletion & legal hold: once data is scheduled for deletion it goes through a soft-delete period (30 days) for recovery unless a legal hold is in place. Legal holds suspend deletion until the hold is released.

I’ve attached a concise playbook (evidence_export_playbook_v1.pdf) and a small sample CSV (audit_export_sample.csv) so you can see column layout. Ben — can you add any throughput/ops notes about expediting a managed archive if the customer has an active Dedicated contract?

Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through this — available late afternoon today.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Security Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: audit log export for security incident forensic review

Laid out well — a couple add-ons from ops:

- If Greenbridge is on Dedicated, we can prioritize the job and reduce turnaround to ~6–12 hours for windows under 90 days.
- For hosted customers who purchase the 1-year cold-archive add-on, we can perform direct S3 streaming which avoids the 24–72h spool step in many cases.
- We’ll redact auth tokens server-side. If they need raw prompt_text for triage we require an approved Data Access request form + an entry in the export_manifest that includes the approver and timestamp.

I’ll attach the signed manifest example for Jake — ops will generate a real manifest during the job.

Ben Carter
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Laura / Ben —

Thanks, that covers most of our questions. Two quick follow-ups:

1) Can you trigger a managed archive for 2026-07-15 -> 2026-07-22 and deliver to our S3 bucket (greenbridge-forensics-us-east-1) as presigned PUT? We’ll share a short-lived write-only presigned URL.

2) For the sample CSV, could you confirm whether caller_ip is obfuscated/anonymized in the sample? Our forensics team needs raw IPs. If you require a Data Access request, we’ll start that immediately.

Let us know a proposed ETA for the job and we’ll get the presigned URL over. If useful we can do a 20-minute call tomorrow 10:00–10:30 PT.

— Jake
